text.p: - Slovenians think the government should spend more on healthcare and education, an annual opinion poll by the Centre for Public Opinion and Media Research showed.
- Electricity distribution company Eles on Monday demanded a 9.6 percent increase of electricity prices from January 1 1997 and a 9.6 percent rise from March 1.

- President Milan Kucan starts the second round of talks with representatives of parliamentary parties on Tuesday to decide the candidate for the new prime minister. A candidate must be named by January 3, 1997.
- Average monthly gross wages in October rose to 135,595 tolars ($954.9), a 2.8 percent increase on September, Slovenia's Statistical Office reported on Monday.
- Construction of a new 20,000 square metre (yards) fair ground in northeastern Maribor is expected to start soon and is due to be completed by the end of the next year.
- Slovenian Minister of Transport, Igor Umek, on Monday signed an agreement for the construction of a road linking Barcelona and Kiev, which will pass through Slovenia.
- President Milan Kucan on Monday met the new Croatian ambassador to Slovenia, Ivica Mastruko, to discuss future cooperation between the two countries.
